results.raw: False. Indian High Court Judgments (AWS Open Data) is not an official publisher; only the issuing High Court’s own official website or authorized reporter constitutes the authoritative source.
False. The Supreme Court of India has not issued any judgment dated 03-02-2026; future dates are impossible.
True. The Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (APTEL) is the statutory appellate body under the Electricity Act, 2003, and Appeal No. 74 of 2008 was indeed filed and decided by it.
True. The Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) is the competent forum for service disputes involving central government employees in India.
False. The Competition Commission of India (CCI) does not issue orders under the style “Case No. 36/2025,” and no such case involving Preeti Kodwani v. Sundar Pichai exists as of 2026-01-05.
True. The Customs, Excise & Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT) is the competent Indian appellate body for customs/excise disputes, and the cited citation matches its official reporting style.
False. The identifier 'CR. WJC/144/2026' cannot match a 2025 judgment; the year suffix is inconsistent.
False. The identifier 'ESCR010000402027' does not correspond to 'C. VELUSAMY versus K INDHERA' (2026-02-03) in the AWS Open Data collection of Indian Supreme Court Judgments.
False. Islamabad High Court is in Pakistan, not India, so it cannot publish an Indian legal decision.
False. Supreme Court Online Bulletin does not publish CAT decisions like O.A./3243/2015; such orders appear on the Central Administrative Tribunal’s official website.
False. The Competition Commission of India (CCI) does not issue orders under the style "Case No. 36/2025"; its numbering follows a different format and 2025 cases cannot pre-date 2023.
False. The Customs, Excise & Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT) does not publish decisions under the prefix “E/”; that format belongs to the Central Excise bench, not CESTAT.
